FEATURE: Brighton and Arsenal meet on the injury line

The next Premier League fixture is Brighton v Arsenal on Saturday morning, and the useful pre-match question is not whether either side has absences but which absences change the structure. Arsenal have a positive read on Ben White and Jurrien Timber, but William Saliba remains out; Brighton carry a longer list into the meeting, including Yankuba Minteh’s two-to-three-month ankle and leg absence.

Mikel Arteta’s Friday update put White and Timber on the positive side of the ledger, with Piero Hincapie and Cristhian Mosquera also expected to train; Saliba remains out (Fantasy Football Scout, https://www.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/2026/09/18/fpl-gameweek-5-team-news-fridays-live-injury-updates-3).

Brighton’s Femi Azeez, Mats Wieffer, Jack Hinshelwood, Minteh, Evan Ferguson, Kaoru Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas and Zadok Yohanna were listed out; Hadjam was considered able to play after a midweek knock (Fantasy Football Scout, https://www.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/2026/09/18/fpl-gameweek-5-team-news-fridays-live-injury-updates-3; Read Arsenal, https://readarsenal.com/2026/09/18/brighton-arsenal-team-news-hadjam-injury/).

The next card also carries live team-news risk elsewhere: Chelsea’s Joao Pedro missed Brazil duty with an injury before Brentford, while Manchester United assess Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba for Fulham (Yahoo Sports, https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/breaking-chelsea-hit-major-injury-144500527.html; RotoWire, https://www.rotowire.com/soccer/headlines/ryan-sessegnon-injury-late-fitness-call-534265).

RANKINGS_NOTES: Opta and the market disagree most sharply about Chelsea: the Opta Power Rankings have them ninth in the world and only England's fifth-best side, behind Liverpool and Manchester United, while the market treats Chelsea as England's third strongest title contender after a winning start to the season.

Everton are the other clear split. Opta rates them inside the world's top 20 on the strength of last season's underlying numbers, yet the market's list of title contenders runs through Brentford, Aston Villa, Brighton and Newcastle without mentioning Everton at all.

Aston Villa and Newcastle move the other way: the market has pushed both out after summer squad losses, while Opta still keeps them 12th and 11th in the world, i.e. above every English club except the Arsenal-City-Liverpool-United-Chelsea group.

Bands follow each competition's current allocation as published alongside the table: four Champions League places in Spain and Italy (plus one Europa and one Conference), and in France, Netherlands, Portugal and Germany the top places include qualifying-round entries rather than guaranteed league-phase spots.

The Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Eredivisie and Primeira Liga are 18-team leagues with two automatic relegations plus a relegation play-off; that play-off place is banded 'playoff' here, so 'playoff' means a promotion/relegation play-off in Europe and MLS Cup Playoffs qualification in MLS.

MLS is the 2026 calendar-year season in its closing stretch, shown as two conferences. The playoff band covers positions 1-9 in each conference: 1-7 enter Round One directly and 8-9 enter the Wild Card matches.
